lesson_title: Why There Are So Few Lions: The Leaky Bucket
hook_text: The Kruger has endless grass and only about 1 600 lions. The reason is a bucket with a hole in it.
clip_script: Grass, arrow, impala, arrow, lion. The arrow points to the eater, because it shows where the energy goes. Now carry the energy in a bucket. The grass holds 10 000 kilojoules. The impala eat it, but by the time it is stored in impala bodies, nine tenths has leaked out. 1000 left. The lions eat the impala. Nine tenths leaks again. 100 left. One more level would get 10, then 1. Nobody can live on that, so chains stop at three or four links and there are fewer animals every step up. A pyramid. Where does it leak? Roots and thorns nobody eats. Dung that was never digested. And most of all respiration: running, breathing, staying warm, leaving as heat. Energy is never destroyed, just spread out where nobody can eat it. That is why a field of maize feeds ten times more people as pap than as beef. Ten percent per step. That is the whole bush.
visual_style: Three buckets in a row labelled grass, impala, lion, each a tenth the size of the last, dripping heat-waves; the drips collect into a pyramid outline.
pacing: Quick chain, slow bucket count, rapid list of leaks, one-line landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any food web like a map.
